𝗔𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗨𝗦𝗘 𝗠𝗢𝗩𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗢 𝗜𝗠𝗣𝗘𝗔𝗖𝗛 𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔, 𝗔𝗞𝗕𝗔𝗬𝗔𝗡 𝗦𝗔𝗬𝗦: “𝗦𝗘𝗘 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗔𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗘𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗘”

Members of Akbayan Party staged a protest on Monday morning outside the House of Representatives in Quezon City on the same day Congress is expected to vote to impeach Vice President Sara Duterte over allegations of undeclared wealth, suspicious multi-billion-peso bank transactions, questionable use of confidential funds, and other serious charges.

The Akbayan advocates gathered at the south gate of Congress holding placards and banners calling on lawmakers to vote in favor of impeachment and demand accountability from the Vice President. During the action, protesters also unfurled a large banner that read: “Sara, See You at the Senate!”

Akbayan Youth National Secretary-General Deeann Caspe said the protest reflects growing public clamor for accountability and the belief that impeachment is now inevitable. “Today, Vice President Sara is poised to go down in Philippine history as the highest-ranking official to be impeached by Congress twice in succession. She should now prepare to face the impeachment court. Sara, see you at the Senate!” he said.

Caspe noted that even if the Supreme Court voided Duterte’s 2025 House impeachment, lawmakers had already voted in large numbers to impeach the Vice President then, and are poised to do so again now. “If the first time left room for doubt, this time the sheer weight, seriousness, and truthfulness of the charges are confirmed,” he added.

Akbayan Representative Perci Cendaña, who joined the protest, said the impending impeachment signals that the long-held perception that holding the Vice President accountable so close to an election is improbable is no longer true. “The math is simple. Every day Sara evades the charges, public distrust deepens and more lawmakers are emboldened to vote for impeachment. Sara herself has become the single biggest force driving Congress to impeach her,” he said.

The Akbayan lawmaker also called on their counterparts in the Senate to proceed “forthwith” in constituting themselves as an impeachment court to hear the case against the vice president, examine the evidence, and ultimately rule on her conviction. It was reported that Akbayan Representative Chel Diokno is being eyed to be part of the House prosecution team.

“There is more than enough probable cause. The evidence against Sara is compelling,” Cendaña said. “I call on our counterparts in the Senate to fulfill their constitutional duty and proceed with the impeachment trial. Congress has done its part. It is now the Senate’s turn to deliver,” Cendaña said. 

#AkbayanPartylist

Militant groups led by Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (BAYAN) and Akbayan hold a protest in front of the House of Representatives in Quezon City on Monday, May 11, in time with the House plenary vote on Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment.

The protesters called on members of the House of Representatives to vote in favor of the impeachment over the alleged misuse of confidential funds and the alleged death threats made by Duterte against the country’s top officials. 

📸: Santi San Juan/MB
